# prepare runs its stages inside a git-dependency build

## Context

The Fleet Manager's Electron packaging (`neomjs/neo-agent-institution` `harness/pack.mjs`) stages the organism and runs `npm install` on a generated manifest that pins the engine by commit: `neo.mjs: github:neomjs/neo#d85060795d8abc99a7d6186968a35e9b8b77188b`. On 2026-09-25 that install failed:

```
npm error code: 'EEXIST', syscall: 'symlink',
npm error path: '../../node_modules/neo-agent-skills/.agents/skills/architecture-pre-flight',
npm error dest: '/Users/Shared/…/neo-agent-institution/harness/.stage/organism/.claude/skills/architecture-pre-flight'
```

The stage root had gained `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills/*` symlinks it never asked for, dangling (the stage's own `node_modules/neo-agent-skills` was not installed yet). Observation and inference are separated below.

## The Problem

`buildScripts/util/prepare.mjs` is the engine's `prepare` lifecycle: husky, then `neo-agent-skills-materialize`. Its header says the materializer runs from `prepare` "never from `postinstall`: npm runs a dependency's `postinstall` inside every consumer's install … while a registry or tarball install never runs `prepare`" (`prepare.mjs:28-31`). That sentence is true for registry installs and false for **git-dependency installs**: npm builds a git dependency by cloning it to a cache directory and running its `prepare` there — with `INIT_CWD` set to the directory the top-level `npm install` was invoked from, i.e. the **consumer's** root.

The materializer resolves its target as `args.root || consumerRoot()`, and `consumerRoot()` returns `INIT_CWD` when set (`neo-agent-skills/scripts/materialize-harness-skills.mjs`, `consumerRoot`). So an engine pinned as `github:neomjs/neo#<sha>` materializes the engine's skills façade into whatever directory installed it. In the Institution's stage that root also receives the brain's `postinstall` materialization (the second git dependency, `neo-agent-brain#8e09275`, declares `postinstall: neo-agent-skills-materialize`); npm runs the two in parallel, and the loser of the rm→mkdir→symlink race exits with EEXIST. Every consumer that pins the engine by commit gets the façade written into its root on install; the race only makes it loud.

Falsifier run (2026-09-25, same tree): `npm_config_ignore_scripts=true node pack.mjs` — the stage completes, `@electron/rebuild` rebuilds the natives, `organism staged … (rebuilt=true)`, exit 0. Nothing else in the install depends on the engine's `prepare`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/util/prepare.mjs` — `runPrepare({root, env, spawnFn})` returns `{skipped, stage, status}`; the only guard today is `npm_config_package_lock_only === 'true'` → `{skipped: 'package-lock-only'}`. Both stages spawn with `cwd: root`.
- The stages provision the engine's **own checkout**: husky writes the checkout's git hooks, the materializer projects the checkout's `.agents/skills` + `.claude/skills`. Neither has a meaning inside a consumer's `node_modules` or a cache clone.
- npm sets `INIT_CWD` for every lifecycle script to the invoking directory; a `prepare` running in the engine's own checkout sees `INIT_CWD === repoRoot` (also under `npm ci`, `npm install`, `npm run prepare` from the root); a git-dependency build sees a foreign `INIT_CWD`. That is the discriminator — no npm flag or cwd heuristic is needed.
- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/prepare.spec.mjs` pins the lock-only guard, stage order and failure propagation with an injected `spawnFn`; the new guard pins into the same spec.

## The Fix

`runPrepare` gains a second guard beside the lock-only one: when `env.INIT_CWD` is set and does not resolve (realpath, falling back to lexical resolution) to `root`, return `{skipped: 'dependency-build', stage: 'guard', status: 0}` before any stage spawns. Header docs correct the "never runs `prepare`" sentence to name the git-dependency case. Nothing changes for a checkout install: husky and the materializer run exactly as today.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runPrepare` (`buildScripts/util/prepare.mjs`) | npm lifecycle contract (`INIT_CWD`); this ticket | foreign `INIT_CWD` → `skipped: 'dependency-build'`, status 0, no spawn; same or unset `INIT_CWD` → unchanged | none — the guard is total | the file header | red-first spec arms below |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — no ADR governs the prepare lifecycle; ADR 0020 §3 (consumers install the engine as a dependency, no source-tree mixing) is the reason the guard is correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `runPrepare({env: {INIT_CWD: '<other dir>'}, spawnFn})` returns `{skipped: 'dependency-build', stage: 'guard', status: 0}` and `spawnFn` is never called (red on `dev`).
- [ ] `runPrepare({env: {INIT_CWD: <root>}})` and `runPrepare({env: {INIT_CWD: <symlink to root>}})` run both stages as today.
- [ ] `runPrepare({env: {}})` (no `INIT_CWD`) runs both stages as today.
- [ ] The lock-only guard keeps precedence and its exact return shape.
- [ ] Header comment names the git-dependency case; no other file changes.
- [ ] Post-merge, in the Institution: `harness/pack.mjs`'s stage install completes with the engine pinned at a commit that carries this guard (recorded on the Institution pin bump, not here).

## Out of Scope

- The materializer's `INIT_CWD` root resolution in `neomjs/neo-agent-skills` (correct for a consumer's own `postinstall`; the caller is what is wrong here).
- `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`'s `postinstall: neo-agent-skills-materialize` running inside its consumers (defect-noted separately; the Brain's call).
- Making `pack.mjs` ignore lifecycle scripts — the probe used that to falsify the cause, not as the fix; the stage must keep running the natives' install scripts.
